newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Meralco to impose standby power fees.
newsitem.headline: Meralco to impose standby power fees.

text.p: Manila Electric Co, the Philippines' biggest electricity distributor, said on Wednesday it plans to impose a standby charge for industrial customers who ask for back-up power.
A Meralco official told Reuters the firm will submit a petition to the state Energy Regulatory Board (ERB) within the week to impose the standby charge.

"We will now impose charges for industries who will request for back-up capacity. Before there were no charges on top of the per kilowatt-hour cost of electricity. The charges will lead to better utilisation of distribution facilities as most of the back-up power is now under-utilised," the official said.
Meralco will ask the ERB to approve a stand-by charge of 115 or 120 pesos per kilowatt per month depending on the voltage.
At present, there are 43 industries that are being provided by Meralco with 250-megawatts of back-up power. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 fax 8176267
